title: memory-management
description: Learn about memory-management. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: JavaScript automatically manages memory through garbage collection, but understanding how it works helps you write more efficient code and avoid memory leaks. Proper memory management ensures your applications remain responsive and don't crash from memory exhaustion.

JavaScript memory is divided into two main areas: the stack and the heap. The stack stores primitive values and references to objects, while the heap stores objects and dynamic data. Understanding this model helps you write memory-efficient code.

data.title: Stack vs Heap Memory

data.text: JavaScript engines use different garbage collection algorithms to reclaim memory. Modern engines use generational garbage collection with mark-and-sweep algorithms for efficient memory management.

data.title: Mark-and-Sweep Algorithm
data.content: How garbage collection identifies unused memory.
data.code:
Mark-and-Sweep Garbage Collection:

1. Mark Phase
   - Start from "roots" (global objects, stack variables)
   - Mark all reachable objects
   - Follow references recursively
   - All marked objects are "live"

2. Sweep Phase
   - Scan entire heap
   - Reclaim memory from unmarked objects
   - Return memory to free pool

Generational Collection:
- Young Generation: New objects, frequent GC
- Old Generation: Long-lived objects, infrequent GC
- Objects promoted from young to old after surviving

Performance Characteristics:
- Fast for young generation (most objects die young)
- Slower for old generation (fewer objects, more expensive)

data.text: Memory leaks occur when objects remain reachable unintentionally, preventing garbage collection. Common patterns include event listeners, closures, DOM references, and global variables.

data.title: Common Memory Leak Patterns

data.text: Adopt memory-efficient coding patterns to reduce memory pressure and improve performance. These include object pooling, typed arrays, and strategic reuse of objects.

data.title: Object Pooling
data.content: Reuse objects instead of creating new ones.

data.title: Typed Arrays for Numeric Data
data.content: Use typed arrays for memory-efficient numeric data.

data.text: WeakMap and WeakSet allow garbage collection of their keys/values when no other references exist. Use them for caching and metadata storage where appropriate.

data.title: WeakMap for Caching
data.content: Use WeakMap to prevent memory leaks in caches.

data.text: Monitor memory usage to identify leaks and optimize consumption. Use browser DevTools and programmatic APIs to track memory over time.

data.title: Memory Monitoring
Memory Limits
data.text: Browsers have memory limits per tab (typically 1-4GB). Exceeding these limits causes tab crashes. Monitor memory usage and implement cleanup strategies for long-running applications.

terms.definition: Automatic memory management that reclaims memory from objects that are no longer reachable.
Garbage collection algorithm that marks reachable objects and sweeps away unmarked ones.
Data structures that allow garbage collection of their keys/values when no other references exist.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: JavaScript uses stack for primitives/references, heap for objects
Garbage collection uses mark-and-sweep with generational optimization
Common memory leaks: event listeners, closures, DOM references, globals
Use object pooling to reuse objects instead of creating new ones
Use typed arrays for memory-efficient numeric data storage
WeakMap/WeakSet allow garbage collection for caching scenarios
Monitor memory usage to identify leaks and optimize consumption
Clean up event listeners and references to prevent leaks
data.takeaway: Understanding JavaScript memory management helps you write efficient code that avoids memory leaks and remains responsive under memory pressure.
